s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit
salient_findings: Elevation deficit of the right eye
Anomalous band in the right orbit
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle
key_facts: 52-year-old woman
History of long-standing diplopia
Persistent vertical misalignment
Orthotropic in primary position
Elevation deficit of the right eye
Previous surgical excision of anomalous band in right orbit
No improvement in motility after surgery
Diplopia remained stable in primary gaze
MRI of orbits showed unremarkable globes
No measured proptosis
Retroocular fat, optic nerves and sheaths, optic chiasm, and brain parenchyma appeared normal
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion noted medial to the medial rectus muscle

shortlist.label: Brown syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of persistent vertical misalignment and elevation deficit

shortlist.label: Superior oblique tendon syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's history of diplopia and elevation deficit

shortlist.label: Adhesive syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the patient's persistent diplopia and elevation deficit, given the history of previous surgical excision of an anomalous band

shortlist.label: Monocular elevation deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of elevation deficit in one eye is consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Double elevator palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the patient's elevation deficit, although less likely given the lack of other characteristic findings

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of previous surgical excision of an anomalous band in the right orbit, which is consistent with the development of adhesions, and the presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle, which could be an area of adhesion causing the elevation deficit of the right eye.

rejected.label: Brown syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with limited elevation in adduction, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Superior oblique tendon syndrome
rejected.why: Would likely cause torsional diplopia and limited rotation, not specifically mentioned

rejected.label: Monocular elevation deficiency
rejected.why: Could be a consideration but the history of surgical excision and presence of a soft-tissue lesion suggests a more mechanical issue like adhesions

rejected.label: Double elevator palsy
rejected.why: Typically presents with limited elevation in both eyes, which is not the case here as the issue is isolated to the right eye
